pairs: In diebus illis iterum cum turba multa esset,
In those days, again, when there was a great crowd,
and they did not have anything to eat,
quia ecce jam triduo sustinent me,
because, behold, they have persevered with me now for three days,
and they do not have anything to eat.
et si dimisero eos jejunos in domum suam,
And if I were to send them away fasting to their home,
they might faint on the way.”
quidam enim ex eis de longe venerunt.
For some of them came from far away.
Unde illos quis poterit saturare panibus in solitudine?
“From where would anyone be able to obtain enough bread for them in the wilderness?”
Et præcepit turbæ discumbere super terram.
And he instructed the crowd to sit down to eat on the ground.
et dabat discipulis suis ut apponerent,
he broke and gave it to his disciples in order to place before them.
And they placed these before the crowd.
And they had a few small fish.
and he ordered them to be placed before them.
et sustulerunt quod superaverat de fragmentis,
And they took up what had been leftover from the fragments:
Erant autem qui manducaverunt, quasi quatuor millia:
And those who ate were about four thousand.
Et statim ascendens navim cum discipulis suis,
And promptly climbing into a boat with his disciples,
he went into the parts of Dalmanutha.
and began to contend with him,
quærentes ab illo signum de cælo,
seeking from him a sign from heaven,
ait: Quid generatio ista signum quærit?
he said: “Why does this generation seek a sign?
if only a sign will be given to this generation!”
he climbed into the boat again,
and he went away across the sea.
And they forgot to take bread.
et nisi unum panem non habebant secum in navi.
And they did not have any with them in the boat, except one loaf.
and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees
and of the leaven of Herod.”
And they discussed this with one another,
“Why do you consider that it is because you have no bread?
Do you not yet know or understand?
Do you still have blindness in your heart?
Having eyes, do you not see?
And having ears, do you not hear?
quando quinque panes fregi in quinque millia:
when I broke the five loaves among the five thousand,
how many baskets full of fragments you took up?”
Quando et septem panes in quatuor millia:
“And when the seven loaves were among the four thousand,
how many baskets of fragments did you take up?”
“How is it that you do not yet understand?”
And they brought a blind man to him.
et rogabant eum ut illum tangeret.
And they petitioned him, so that he would touch him.
And taking the blind man by the hand,
he led him beyond the village.
et exspuens in oculos ejus impositis manibus suis,
And putting spit on his eyes, laying his hands on him,
he asked him if he could see anything.
“I see men but they are like walking trees.”
Deinde iterum imposuit manus super oculos ejus:
Next he placed his hands again over his eyes,
et restitutus est ita ut clare videret omnia.
And he was restored, so that he could see everything clearly.
Et misit illum in domum suam,
And he sent him to his house,
and if you enter into the town,
And Jesus departed with his disciples into the towns of Caesarea Philippi.
et discipuli ejus in castella Cæsareæ Philippi:
et in via interrogabat discipulos suos,
“Who do men say that I am?”
And they answered him by saying:
alii vero quasi unum de prophetis.
still others perhaps one of the prophets.”
Vos vero quem me esse dicitis?
who do you say that I am?”
Peter responded by saying to him,
not to tell anyone about him.
Et cœpit docere eos quoniam oportet Filium hominis pati multa,
And he began to teach them that the Son of man must suffer many things,
and be rejected by the elders,
and after three days rise again.
And he spoke the word openly.
And turning away and looking at his disciples,
quoniam non sapis quæ Dei sunt,
for you do not prefer the things that are of God,
but the things that are of men.”
Et convocata turba cum discipulis suis,
And calling together the crowd with his disciples,
Qui enim voluerit animam suam salvam facere,
For whoever will have chosen to save his life,
qui autem perdiderit animam suam propter me,
But whoever will have lost his life,
for my sake and for the Gospel,
For how does it benefit a man,
if he gains the whole world,
and yet causes harm to his soul?
Aut quid dabit homo commutationis pro anima sua?
Or, what will a man give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever has been ashamed of me and of my words,
et verba mea in generatione ista adultera
among this adulterous and sinful generation,
the Son of man also will be ashamed of him,
when he will arrive in the glory of his Father,
cum venerit in gloria Patris sui cum angelis sanctis.
quia sunt quidam de hic stantibus, qui non gustabunt mortem donec videant regnum Dei veniens in virtute.
that there are some among those standing here who shall not taste death until they see the kingdom of God arriving in power.”
